prompt:
In a checkpoint-enabled clone, plain git maintenance commands have started misbehaving: `git fetch --all` and `git remote update` now try to contact every checkpoint URL the repository has ever fetched from - including long-dead mirror hosts and internal SSH URLs - which makes those bulk commands slow and prone to hard errors when any of those hosts is unreachable.

The cause traces back to how Entire pulls checkpoints: each filtered checkpoint fetch appears to leave its own `remote.<url>.*` section behind in the clone's `.git/config`, and git then treats each of those sections as just another fetchable remote, so `--all` / `remote update` dial all of them.

Make bulk fetch/update operations stop reaching out to these accumulated per-checkpoint entries. The constraint: normal on-demand object fetching for filtered checkpoints (pulling in objects that were filtered out at fetch time) must keep working exactly as before, and a normal unfiltered fetch must not start leaving new config sections behind either. Only the bulk-fetch behavior should change.
brain_queries: git fetch --all and git remote update dial every checkpoint URL ever fetched from including dead hosts
filtered checkpoint fetch leaves leftover promisor remote entries in .git/config treated as fetchable remotes
should checkpoint fetches reuse a named git remote instead of fetching by raw URL
avoid git persisting promisor and partial-clone settings that alter user fetch and pull behavior
URL-based filtered fetch versus fetching by remote name git config mutation
_subject: checkpoint fetch: exclude URL-keyed promisor entries from bulk git fetch --all rather than switching to a named remote
_rolling_cutoff_confidence: no_checkpoint (commit has no Entire-Checkpoint trailer; not an Entire session; 0 provenance sessions touch expected_files within +/-1d -> nothing to leak; cutoff guards temporality)
